extracted.intended_audience: peer reviewers of EPSRC research proposals using the Je-S system (UKRI reviewers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for reviewers completing peer review reports for EPSRC grant proposals via the Je-S system (transitioning to UKRI Funding Service). Covers assessment criteria, expected tone and content of reports, procedural requirements and timescales.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment criterion: quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality (one of four core assessment criteria). "Quality remains the pre-eminent assessment criterion for all proposals."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat scientific/technical quality as the primary criterion when assessing proposals. Quality should carry the greatest weight relative to the other core criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment criterion: importance
rubrics_metrics.description: Importance (one of four core assessment criteria). "Importance also plays a major role in the assessment process."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing Importance, reviewers are asked to comment explicitly on the strategic fit of the proposal with respect to the portfolio EPSRC is trying to create. Include comment on how the proposed research relates to EPSRC research areas and any strategic actions highlighted in them, and on where a successful research programme would position the UK in the global research landscape, identifying the international leaders in the area.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment criterion: applicant and partnerships
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant and partnerships (one of four core assessment criteria).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the suitability, track record and capacity of the applicant(s) and the strength, appropriateness and added value of any partnerships or collaborators. Refer to scheme-specific guidance where available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment criterion: resources and management
rubrics_metrics.description: Resources and management (one of four core assessment criteria).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether requested resources are appropriate and justified and whether the management plan and infrastructure are adequate to deliver the proposed work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refer to scheme-specific criteria and application guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Some schemes may have additional scheme-specific criteria. "You should always refer to the specific guidance."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before reviewing, check the call document and any scheme-specific guidance (and the application guidance for individual EPSRC funding opportunities). Tailor comments to any additional or bespoke criteria for that call or scheme.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good reviewing: clarity and concision
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer reports should "provide clear and concise comments and recommendations."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write succinct, readable reports focused on the key strengths, weaknesses and recommendations so panels and applicants can readily understand and act on them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good reviewing: identify strengths and weaknesses
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer reports should "clearly identify strengths and weaknesses."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly list or describe the strongest and weakest aspects of the proposal, linking these to the assessment criteria and to any overall scores or recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good reviewing: justify overall markings
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer reports should "give justification for overall markings."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide evidence and reasoning that support any numerical scores, overall ratings or funding recommendations so panels can understand the basis for your judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good reviewing: raise concerns as questions for the applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer reports should "raise concerns in the form of questions for the applicant."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame uncertainties or issues as clear questions to allow the applicant to respond to factual inaccuracies or to clarify points during the rebuttal/response stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good reviewing: provide constructive criticism
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer actionable suggestions for improvement where appropriate rather than simply negative statements; aim to help applicants strengthen proposals in future iterations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer conduct: timeliness, objectivity, fairness and being informed
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer comments should be "timely, objective, fair and informed."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you cannot meet the indicated timescale, confirm immediately so an alternative reviewer can be sought or the deadline extended. Also confirm immediately if you do not feel qualified to comment. Ensure reviews are impartial, evidence-based and informed by relevant expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential comments policy and feedback process
rubrics_metrics.description: The process is open and confidential comments will be withheld from applicants only in exceptional circumstances. "Your report will be fed back anonymously to the applicant, who will then be allowed to respond to factual inaccuracies or questions you raise."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely on confidential-only feedback except in exceptional cases; reports are normally shared (anonymously) with applicants who may respond, and panels will use your reports as a chief tool for prioritisation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural requirement: submit reviews via Je-S
rubrics_metrics.description: All reviews requested by EPSRC must be completed through the research councils’ Je-S system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the electronic forms available through Je-S to submit reviews. PDF/downloadable versions of forms and guidance are available if you prefer to work offline; you may cut-and-paste from an offline copy into Je-S when ready. Follow the specific reviewer form tailored to the proposal type (standard, fellowships, networks, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Awareness of how reports are used
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports are used to distinguish between proposals: "members of prioritisation panels will be asked to use your reports as the chief tool for distinguishing between proposals."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that your assessments and evidence will directly influence funding decisions; structure your report to make its implications for prioritisation clear.
